overview:
**High fire danger continues today, driven by persistently dry fuels (ERC 82%) despite scattered thunderstorm chances.**
- Danger stays High all seven days, with ERC easing to the low-70s midweek before climbing back to 82% by August 19 as humidity trends downward.
- Key driver this week is fading moisture: max humidity drops from 84% today to 60% by August 19, with winds shifting from ENE to NE.
- No Red Flag Warning is active for this area today, and 0 of 7 local watchout thresholds are currently met.
- Stage 2 Fire Restrictions are in effect on the Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forests, alongside Stage 2 restrictions in Montrose, San Miguel, and Delta counties.
- The Gold Mountain Fire near Ouray is 39,605 acres and 90% contained; the Elk Fire near Lake City continues to be managed with an incident management team assigned, now at 7,404 acres and 35% contained per today's report.
